# Job Chapter 20 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 423r–423v

---

**1** Then Zophar the Naamathite replied:

**2** "My racing thoughts force me to respond — the turmoil inside me will not let me stay quiet. **3** I have heard a rebuke that insults me, and something deeper than mere understanding compels me to answer.

**4** Surely you know this — it has been true since the beginning of time, since human beings were first placed on the earth: **5** the triumph of the wicked is short-lived, and the joy of the godless lasts only a moment.

**6** Even if his arrogance rises to the heavens and his head touches the clouds, **7** he will vanish forever — like his own waste. People who knew him will ask, 'Where did he go?'

**8** He will fly away like a dream and never be found — scattered like a vision in the night. **9** The eye that once saw him will never see him again. Even the place where he lived will not recognize him.

**10** His children will beg from the poor. His own hands will have to return what he stole. **11** The strength of youth that fills his bones will end up lying with him in the dirt.

**12** Evil may taste sweet in his mouth — he may savor it, rolling it around under his tongue, **13** reluctant to let it go, holding it like a delicacy —

**14** but that food will turn sour in his stomach. It will become cobra venom inside him.

**15** He gorges himself on riches, then vomits them up. God will force them out of his stomach. **16** He will drink the poison of cobras. A viper's fangs will kill him.

**17** He will never enjoy the sight of flowing streams — rivers of honey and cream. **18** He will have to give back everything he worked for without ever enjoying it. The profits from his business will bring him no pleasure.

**19** Because he crushed and abandoned the poor, because he seized houses he never built,

**20** because he never knew a moment of contentment — always wanting more — he will not escape with any of his treasures. **21** Nothing will be left for him to consume. His prosperity will not last.

**22** At the peak of his abundance, distress will strike. The full weight of misery will crash down on him.

**23** When he has filled his belly, God will unleash burning anger against him and rain down wrath on him as he eats.

**24** He may flee from an iron weapon, but a bronze arrow will pierce him. **25** The shaft is pulled out; the gleaming point emerges from his body. Terrors overwhelm him.

**26** Total darkness is stored up for everything he treasured. A fire no one lit will consume him. It will devour whatever survives in his tent.

**27** The heavens will expose his guilt, and the earth will rise up as a witness against him. **28** The wealth of his household will be swept away — poured out on the day of God's wrath.

**29** This is what God assigns to the wicked. This is the inheritance God has decreed for them."

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**The body as metaphor:** Zophar's speech is built around the body — specifically, the stomach. Evil is tasted (v.12), savored (v.13), swallowed (v.15), digested into poison (v.14), and vomited up (v.15). Wealth is consumed and expelled. The wicked man's greed is physical, and so is its punishment. The metaphor says something profound: what you take in shapes what you become, and what you become destroys you.

**The short triumph (vv.4-9):** Zophar's argument is that the success of the wicked is real but brief. This is actually more nuanced than Bildad's position — Zophar admits the wicked do prosper, but insists the prosperity is temporary. The problem, of course, is that "temporary" could mean a full lifetime, which Job will point out in chapter 21.

**"A fire not fanned" (v.26):** Supernatural fire — divine judgment that needs no human cause. The echo of Sodom is unmistakable. Zophar is warning that the wicked man's fate is not merely natural consequence but active divine destruction.

*— PNEUMA*
